Part 2

Levels of Biological Organization

Life is a hierarchy: each level builds on the one below. Press → to zoom out one level at a time.

Key idea

Emergent properties

At each level, new properties emerge that are not present in the parts alone.

💧 Water (H₂O) has properties that neither hydrogen nor oxygen has alone.

🫀 A single heart-muscle cell contracts — but only an organized organ pumps blood.

🧠 Billions of neurons together produce thought — no single neuron “thinks”.

Part 3

Cell Theory

1

All living things are made of cells.

2

The cell is the basic unit of structure and function.

3

All cells arise from pre-existing cells.

📜 Schleiden (1838, plants) · Schwann (1839, animals) · Virchow (1855): “Omnis cellula e cellula” — every cell from a cell.

Types of organisms

One cell or many?

Unicellular

A single cell carries out all essential functions of life: metabolism, growth and reproduction. e.g. bacteria, amoeba, yeast.

Multicellular

Many specialised cells organised into tissues — connective, epithelial, muscle and nervous tissue. e.g. humans.

Two types of cells

Prokaryotic vs Eukaryotic

Prokaryotes

pro = before · karyon = nucleus

  • No membrane-bound nucleus
  • Circular chromosome in the nucleoid
  • Bacteria & Archaea

Eukaryotes

eu = true · karyon = nucleus

  • True membrane-bound nucleus
  • Membrane-bound organelles
  • Animals, plants, fungi, protists

🧂 Halobacterium — an archaeon (prokaryote) that thrives in extremely salty lakes and colours them pink.

Zoom in

The Prokaryotic (Bacterial) Cell

🧬 Nucleoid: essential genes on a single circular chromosome in the cytoplasm — no nuclear membrane.

📎 Fimbriae & pili: hair-like structures that attach the cell to surfaces or to other cells (some pili also transfer DNA).

🌀 Flagellum: a whip-like tail that rotates to move the cell.

🛡️ Most bacteria have a cell wall outside the plasma membrane; ribosomes are free in the cytoplasm.

Part 4

The 7 Characteristics of Living Systems

Characteristic · Regulation

Homeostasis

Maintaining a stable internal environment while the external environment changes. Move the slider ↓

Outside temperature

22°C
❄️ −10🔥 48

Core body temperature

37°C

(≈ 98.6 °F) — kept almost constant by negative feedback.

Characteristic · Growth

Growth & Development

Individual cells become larger, and multicellular organisms accumulate many cells through cell division.

Press Divide and watch one cell become many: 1 cell(s).

📈 After n divisions → 2ⁿ cells. The human body: ~37 trillion cells ≈ 2⁴⁵!

Characteristic · Energy processing

Metabolism

The total of all biochemical reactions in an organism = anabolism + catabolism.

🏗️ Anabolism

Builds complex molecules from simpler ones. Requires energy (from ATP).
e.g. amino acids → protein

🔨 Catabolism

Breaks down complex molecules into simpler ones. Releases energy.
e.g. glucose → CO₂ + H₂O

⚡ QUICK CHECK · SORT IT

Anabolism or catabolism?

Photosynthesis (making glucose)Cellular respirationDNA replication Digesting starch into glucoseBuilding muscle proteinBreaking down fats for energy

🏗️ Anabolism (builds, uses energy)

🔨 Catabolism (breaks, releases energy)

Characteristic · Response

Response to Stimuli

Organisms show irritability — they respond to changes in their environment (we pull our hand away from a flame — fast!). Test your response:

👆

Click here to start

Wait for GREEN, then click as fast as you can.

Your best time

—

👁️ Stimulus (light) → eye → brain → muscles → response (click). A typical visual reaction time is roughly 200–300 ms.

Characteristic · Reproduction & heredity

Reproduction

Living organisms produce new organisms and pass on their genetic information (DNA).

Asexual — one parent

Offspring are genetically identical clones. e.g. bacterial binary fission.

Sexual — two parents

Gametes (sperm + egg) fuse → offspring with new combinations of genes.

Characteristic · Evolutionary adaptation

Evolution in action

The genetic makeup of a population changes over time. Birds spot green beetles more easily on brown soil. Run the generations!

Generation 0

🟩 Green 50% · 🟫 Brown 50%

💡 No beetle “decided” to change colour. Variation already existed; the environment selected which variants survived to reproduce.

The Scientific Method

Press → to walk through a real example: Does light affect seedling growth?

✅ Science is evidence-based and self-correcting.

Experiment design

Variables & controls

🎛️

Independent variable

What the scientist changes.
Amount of light.

📏

Dependent variable

What is measured.
Seedling height (cm).

🔒

Controlled variables

Kept the same.
Water, soil, seed type, temperature.

⚖️

Control group

The baseline for comparison.
Seedlings in normal light.

In the seedling experiment, the dark group was also kept 5 °C colder. What's the problem?

💬 CRITICAL THINKING DEBATE

Are viruses alive?

Vote first — then reveal the arguments and use the checklist of life.

✅ Arguments for “alive”

Contain genetic material (DNA or RNA) · replicate (inside hosts) · evolve by natural selection.

❌ Arguments against

No cells · no metabolism of their own · cannot reproduce or maintain homeostasis outside a host cell.

🧠 Most biologists place viruses at the edge of life. The real lesson: definitions in science are tools — they are tested and refined by evidence.

Wrap-up

Summary of Key Concepts

🔬 Biology = the study of life and living systems.

🔄 Life is defined by organization, regulation, growth, metabolism, response, reproduction and evolution.

🧪 The scientific method is the foundation of all biological investigation.

🪜 Life is organized in hierarchical levels with emergent properties.
